newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY MAIZE FUTURES UP, WHEAT HOPES SERBIA SALES.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY MAIZE FUTURES UP, WHEAT HOPES SERBIA SALES.

text.p: Maize futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange firmed on Friday amid position liquidations, while milling wheat futures rose on rumours about potential export sales to Serbia, traders said.

March maize ended up by 300 forints at 17,900 forints per tonne. July, October and December maize futures also firmed by 100 to 300 forints, to close at 17,000, 18,000 and 18,750 forints respectively.

"The speculative liquidation of positions drives up the prices, and also most players do not want to deliver the crop," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle Rt, adding that in the longer-term large carry-over stocks from 1996 were likely to put maize prices under pressure.

Traders said that wheat futures, which fell much recently on over 500,000 tonnes of 1996 crop for which traders did not see buyers, rose on Friday due to market talks that Serbia was likely to need substantial amount of import wheat.
"The rumour has spread that there is outlook for large-volume export to Serbia," Herczeg said, adding he had no evidence that the news were true.

Traders said some mills stopped production as the storing of flower caused difficulties to some of them due to large stocks, and this was likely to push wheat prices further down if new export markets would not open soon.
Milling wheat futures firmed by 200 to 400 forints per tonne. The May maturity rose to 23,460 forints, up 400, and December wheat also finished up by 400 forints, at 21,500.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
